title: Burst Pool Sizing Model (Dedicated Burst Pools) — v0.6
content:
Redwood Inference — Dedicated Burst Capacity
Burst pool sizing spreadsheet (text export)

Purpose
- Quantify per-region burst pool size (GPU count) needed to support Dedicated tenant spikes.
- Keep Hosted commitments protected via hard headroom allocations + saturation gates.
- Provide sensitivity analysis to inform pilot vs GA capacity commits.

Version notes
- v0.6: updated spike multipliers from customer interviews (PM-641), added cooldown effect approximation, added EU split (eu-west-1 vs eu-central-1) and L40S pool option.
- TODO: incorporate observed burst admission SLO metrics from pilot game-day (when available).

--------------------------------------------
TAB: Overview

Definitions
- Baseline Dedicated capacity: capacity reserved for a Dedicated tenant’s committed throughput.
- Burst pool: controlled shared pool capacity that Dedicated tenants can temporarily borrow.
- “Burst-eligible demand”: demand above baseline that is allowed to attempt admission to burst.

High-level approach
1) Forecast burst-eligible incremental demand (in tokens/sec and concurrency) per region/GPU.
2) Convert incremental demand -> required GPUs using conservative effective TPS per GPU.
3) Apply safety multipliers (variance + warmup + partial outages).
4) Cap by infra-committed burst headroom per region (hard allocation) and validate hosted protection.

Sizing formula (simplified)
Required_GPUs = CEIL( (P95_Incremental_TPS / Effective_TPS_per_GPU) * Safety_Margin )

Where:
- P95_Incremental_TPS = (Baseline_P95_TPS * Spike_Multiplier - Baseline_P95_TPS) * Burst_Enabled_Share
- Effective_TPS_per_GPU = Nominal_TPS_per_GPU * Target_Utilization

Assumptions are in the Inputs tab.

--------------------------------------------
TAB: Inputs

Global inputs (default values used for v0.6)
| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Planning window | 30 min | Typical spike duration from interviews; we size to handle 30–45 min without operator action. |
| Burst enabled share (of Dedicated tenants) | 0.35 | Pilot: 2–3 customers; GA forecast: 20–40% opt-in in first 2 quarters. Using 0.35 for “early GA”. |
| Spike multiplier (P95) | 2.8x | Customer interview median for “weekly batch + product launches”; sensitivity table covers 2.0–4.0x. |
| Overlap factor (spike concurrency across tenants) | 0.55 | Probability that spikes overlap in same region; conservative for peak business hours. |
| Target utilization (burst pool) | 0.65 | Keep headroom for tail latency; saturation gate begins at ~0.80. |
| Safety margin | 1.25 | Accounts for variance, model mix, imperfect packing. |
| N-1 allowance | 1.10 | Single node/host failure + maintenance; applied post-conversion. |
| Warm pool fraction | 0.15 | Fraction of GPUs kept warm/spare (driver warm, images pulled) to reduce cold-start latency. |
| Cooldown effectiveness | 0.90 | Approx: cooldown/backoff reduces sustained admission by ~10% under contention (less thrash). |

Per-GPU “effective TPS per GPU” (planning numbers; not vendor benchmarks)
NOTE: These are *planning constants* for sizing; runtime changes may shift these.
| GPU | Workload profile | Nominal TPS/GPU | Target util | Effective TPS/GPU |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100-80G | mixed chat (8k ctx, streaming) | 11,500 | 0.65 | 7,475 |
| A100-80G | mixed chat (8k ctx, streaming) | 7,800 | 0.65 | 5,070 |
| L40S | embeddings + short chat (<=2k ctx) | 4,600 | 0.65 | 2,990 |

Demand composition (default)
| Dimension | Default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Model mix shift during spikes | +10% larger models | Spikes often correlate with “new feature launch” => heavier requests; conservative. |
| Cross-region spill allowed | No (v1) | Keep data residency simple; routing may fail over within region only. |

Hosted protection constraints (hard allocations; infra commit)
- Burst pools must not consume capacity needed to meet Hosted on-demand + contracted Hosted SLAs.
- For v0.6 planning, infra commit is expressed as maximum burst GPUs per region/GPU type.

--------------------------------------------
TAB: Regional Baseline Demand Inputs (as of 2025-06-30)

This tab is normally a feed from internal capacity dashboards; here are the working numbers used.

Baseline Dedicated P95 TPS by region (aggregate across all Dedicated tenants in that region)
| Region | Baseline_P95_TPS | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| us-east-1 | 72,000 | Largest Dedicated footprint; mix includes long-context chat. |
| us-west-2 | 39,000 | Smaller but spikier; more launch traffic. |
| eu-west-1 | 28,000 | Ireland; enterprise demand. |
| eu-central-1 | 19,000 | Frankfurt; data residency customers. |
| ap-southeast-1 | 14,000 | Early APAC; growth expected. |

GPU allocation preference by region (current Dedicated fleet reality)
| Region | Primary GPU for burst pool | Secondary | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| us-east-1 | H100-80G | A100-80G | Most new deployments H100; keep A100 pool small for compatibility. |
| us-west-2 | H100-80G | A100-80G | Similar to us-east-1. |
| eu-west-1 | A100-80G | H100-80G | H100 supply constrained in EU in near term. |
| eu-central-1 | A100-80G | L40S | L40S only for shorter workloads/embeddings; treat as separate pool class. |
| ap-southeast-1 | A100-80G | — | Limited H100 supply. |

--------------------------------------------
TAB: Burst Incremental Demand Calculation

Computation steps (per region)
1) Burst-eligible incremental TPS (P95):
   Incremental_TPS = Baseline_P95_TPS * (Spike_Multiplier - 1) * Burst_Enabled_Share * Overlap_Factor * Cooldown_Effectiveness

Using defaults:
- Spike_Multiplier = 2.8
- Burst_Enabled_Share = 0.35
- Overlap_Factor = 0.55
- Cooldown_Effectiveness = 0.90

Constant factor = (2.8 - 1) * 0.35 * 0.55 * 0.90 = 0.31185
So: Incremental_TPS ≈ Baseline_P95_TPS * 0.31185

Computed Incremental TPS by region (P95)
| Region | Baseline_P95_TPS | Factor | Incremental_P95_TPS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| us-east-1 | 72,000 | 0.31185 | 22,453 |
| us-west-2 | 39,000 | 0.31185 | 12,162 |
| eu-west-1 | 28,000 | 0.31185 | 8,732 |
| eu-central-1 | 19,000 | 0.31185 | 5,925 |
| ap-southeast-1 | 14,000 | 0.31185 | 4,366 |

Notes
- This is not “total burst TPS”; it’s incremental above baseline that attempts admission.
- Admission control may deny some requests; we size to keep deny rates low in normal conditions.

--------------------------------------------
TAB: Pool Size Output (GPUs)

Apply conversion to GPUs and safety margins:
Required_GPUs_raw = CEIL(Incremental_P95_TPS / Effective_TPS_per_GPU)
Required_GPUs = CEIL(Required_GPUs_raw * Safety_Margin * N-1_allowance / (1 - Warm_pool_fraction))

Defaults:
- Safety_Margin = 1.25
- N-1_allowance = 1.10
- Warm_pool_fraction = 0.15
Multiplier = 1.25 * 1.10 / (1 - 0.15) = 1.6176

Region outputs (primary GPU class)
| Region | Primary GPU | Effective TPS/GPU | Incremental_P95_TPS | GPUs_raw | Multiplier | Suggested Pool GPUs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| us-east-1 | H100 | 7,475 | 22,453 | 4 | 1.6176 | 7 |
| us-west-2 | H100 | 7,475 | 12,162 | 2 | 1.6176 | 4 |
| eu-west-1 | A100 | 5,070 | 8,732 | 2 | 1.6176 | 4 |
| eu-central-1 | A100 | 5,070 | 5,925 | 2 | 1.6176 | 4 |
| ap-southeast-1 | A100 | 5,070 | 4,366 | 1 | 1.6176 | 2 |

Total suggested burst pool GPUs (v0.6) = 21 GPUs

Secondary/compat pools (small)
These are used to avoid “no compatible burst pool” when a tenant is pinned to older GPU class.
| Region | Secondary GPU | Suggested Pool GPUs | Rationale |
|---|---|---:|---|
| us-east-1 | A100 | 2 | Compatibility for existing A100 Dedicated tenants; keep tiny to reduce fragmentation. |
| us-west-2 | A100 | 1 | Same. |
| eu-west-1 | H100 | 1 | If H100 supply allows; primarily for next-gen tenants; can be 0 for pilot. |
| eu-central-1 | L40S | 2 | Embeddings/short workloads; explicitly excluded from long-context chat admission policies. |

Infra headroom cap check (hard max; from infra planning thread)
| Region | Primary GPU | Cap (GPUs) | Suggested (GPUs) | Status |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| us-east-1 | H100 | 10 | 7 | OK |
| us-west-2 | H100 | 6 | 4 | OK |
| eu-west-1 | A100 | 6 | 4 | OK |
| eu-central-1 | A100 | 5 | 4 | OK |
| ap-southeast-1 | A100 | 3 | 2 | OK |

Operational notes
- If we cannot keep warm pool fraction at 15% (due to cost pressure), increase admission deny rate expectations or increase total GPUs.
- Pool scaling/warmup time assumptions: 10–15 min to add nodes in cloud regions; therefore warm pool is critical for “burst within minutes” experience.

--------------------------------------------
TAB: Sensitivity Analysis

Sensitivity 1: Spike multiplier
(holding Burst_Enabled_Share=0.35, Overlap=0.55, Cooldown=0.90)
Impact shown as total primary GPUs across all regions (excluding secondary pools).

| Spike Multiplier | Constant factor ((m-1)*0.35*0.55*0.90) | Total Primary GPUs |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2.0x | 0.17325 | 13 |
| 2.5x | 0.25988 | 18 |
| 2.8x (default) | 0.31185 | 21 |
| 3.2x | 0.38115 | 25 |
| 4.0x | 0.51975 | 33 |

Interpretation
- Moving from 2.8x -> 3.2x costs ~4 GPUs across the fleet (mostly in us-east-1 / us-west-2).
- If we see systematic 3.2x spikes in pilot, we should either (a) tighten per-tenant caps, or (b) increase us-east-1/us-west-2 pool sizes first.

Sensitivity 2: Overlap factor
(holding Spike multiplier 2.8x)
| Overlap | Total Primary GPUs | Notes |
|---:|---:|---|
| 0.35 | 16 | Lower overlap = tenants spike at different times (best case). |
| 0.55 (default) | 21 | Realistic for “weekday mornings” clustering. |
| 0.75 | 27 | Worst case: coordinated launch windows. Requires tighter windows/cooldowns or more pool capacity. |

Sensitivity 3: Target utilization
(holding Spike=2.8x)
| Target Utilization | Effective TPS/GPU change | Total Primary GPUs | Notes |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 0.75 | +15% effective | 18 | Riskier tail latency; might violate neighbor p99 drift targets under mix shift. |
| 0.65 (default) | baseline | 21 | Current recommendation. |
| 0.55 | -15% effective | 26 | Safer for latency, more expensive. |

Sensitivity 4: EU H100 supply constraint scenario
- If eu-west-1 remains A100-only through GA, OK (numbers already assume A100 primary).
- If eu-west-1 A100 availability dips, we cannot “borrow” H100 from hosted without violating hosted protection. In that case, prefer:
  1) tighten per-tenant burst TPS caps in EU first
  2) shift some EU customers to eu-central-1 if contract allows
  3) delay EU GA until supply recovers

--------------------------------------------
TAB: Notes / Open Questions

Open questions (needs follow-up with routing + policy)
- Do we size to an admission success SLO (e.g., 99% admitted when pool < 70% utilized) or to a deny-rate target (e.g., <1% denies in steady state)? SRE preference: define explicit “burst admission SLO” per Confluence draft.
- How much should cooldown be credited in sizing? v0.6 uses a simplistic 0.90 factor; might double-count if we also assume lower overlap.
- Do we allow “model variant fallback” (smaller model) to count as successful burst admission? Product says: customer-visible behavior matters; might be acceptable if documented.

Data inputs / hygiene
- Baseline_P95_TPS should be recomputed weekly during pilot (Dedicated growth is fast).
- Need to split Baseline_P95_TPS by GPU class for more accurate compatibility sizing (currently aggregated).

Pilot recommendation (capacity commit)
- Start pilot with:
  - us-east-1: 6 H100 + 2 A100 compat
  - us-west-2: 4 H100
  - eu-west-1: 3 A100
  - eu-central-1: 3 A100
  - ap-southeast-1: 2 A100
- Keep 1–2 GPUs of “buffer” unassigned in us-east-1 if supply allows (for emergency warm pool).

Change log
- 2025-06-08 (Jamal): initial model and rough per-region numbers.
- 2025-06-24 (Keiko): added cooldown factor + warm pool fraction.
- 2025-07-03 (Vanessa): updated region caps based on infra supply check.
- 2025-07-15 (Sean/Rafael): added sensitivity tables for game-day planning and ops readiness.
